To elevate your work for the final submission, focus on defining quantified technical requirements, resolving key astrodynamics principles in your orbit design, incorporating concrete preliminary calculations or simulations, and polishing your academic presentation with complete formal references and consistent scheduling.","next_steps":["Redesign your orbital architecture to reflect correct astrodynamics, replacing the 600 km geostationary concept with a physically viable LEO constellation or repeating ground-track orbit, verified via preliminary calculations or STK.","Define formal, quantitative engineering requirements in your concept section, detailing parameters such as ground sample distance (resolution), spectral bands for coral monitoring, and required revisit frequency.","Refine report consistency and formatting by aligning your narrative text with your Gantt chart milestones, adding figure captions, and converting bare URL links into formal bibliographic citations."],"criteria":{"C1":"In 'Mission Concept & Rationale', you articulated a strong environmental need and clearly identified marine scientists as end users. To reach 'Accomplished', add explicit contingency plans for potential technical delays, clarify how individual tasks connect directly to your mission narrative, and identify specific literature and software sources you plan to use.","C3":"While you identified orbit selection as a priority, claiming a 600 km geostationary orbit violates fundamental orbital mechanics (GEO requires ~35,786 km over the equator). To reach 'Adequate' or 'Accomplished', conduct viable preliminary trade-offs (e.g., LEO vs. GEO), and include concrete technical calculations or preliminary STK simulation results.","C4":"Your report has a clear, readable structure with helpful subheadings.
